chunks: Ahmad narrated from Al-Husayn, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) preferred that when he returned (from a journey) and when he set out (on a journey) in winter, it should be during the night of Friday. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah chose a thing from every thing, so He chose from the days the day of Friday.'

key_terms.يَسْتَحِبُّ: He preferred / He loved to do

ai.seo_question: Why is Friday night considered virtuous in Shia Islam according to the Prophet's practice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the preeminence of Friday night by linking it to the Prophet’s preference for undertaking journeys during this time, a practice reflecting both spiritual preparation and practical wisdom. It reinforces the Shia belief that Allah’s selection of Friday is not arbitrary but a divine choice that elevates its status above all other days, inviting believers to maximize its blessings through specific acts of worship.
